name: Privileged by Design

authors.name: Operation Coinnectar Crew (HaxNation x FOSS Mumbai 2026)

description:
Coinnectar builds on a self-hosted runner tagged privileged. The attacker understood exactly what that grants: a --privileged sandbox shares the host's capabilities and devices, so the wall between “job” and “machine” is thin — if you know where to push.

Stand up the local privileged runner lab (see lab/README.md) and break out of the job sandbox onto the host. The flag sits on the runner host under /opt/ctf/, on a filesystem the sandbox can reach but hasn't been handed.
hints: Being privileged doesn't hand you the host's files — it hands you the host's block devices. List them.
A disk you can see is a disk you can mount. Mount the host's root partition somewhere and read what you need — then look closely at what you recover.

deployment.notes: Local privileged lab. Players run the lab on their own machine; see lab/README.md. Do not run on production hosts.
